annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on digital identity, data sovereignty and the path to a just digital transition for citizens living in the information society
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on digital identity, data sovereignty and the path to a just digital transition for citizens living in the information society
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C 443/22
annotation.summary_en: EESC opinion on the European Digital Identity proposal, data sovereignty and a just digital transition. It urges rights-based regulation, GDPR updates, anti-discrimination, security, accountability for AI malfunctions, a 'human in command' approach, bans on social scoring, EU data storage, and digital literacy. It mentions human control over robots in defence only in passing.
key_provisions_or_claims: Digital ID must remain voluntary, with anti-discrimination provisions and public-body management under democratic control.
Calls for GDPR update and informed consent for personal and non-personal data.
Full accountability for AI malfunctions, with liability on developers and owners; 'human in command' approach.
Opposes private facial recognition databases (except for crime) and social scoring.
Calls for impact assessments, EU data stored on EU soil, and digital literacy programmes.
